Add recorded partner information to union histories

Source: R/get_detailed_unions.R
get_detailed_unions.Rd

Match wives and husbands to the population's person table by ID and return their recorded birth times, death times, and optional groups at formation alongside every union record. Union row order and all existing columns are retained. The population and its union table are not modified. No known endpoint is needed.

Usage

get_detailed_unions(population)

Arguments

population

A validated hammel_population containing person and union histories, such as the result of simulate().

Value

A separate tibble with all union columns plus birth_time_w, death_time_w, birth_time_h, and death_time_h. When group is present, also group_w and group_h. Suffixes _w and _h identify wives and husbands. Empty union histories retain the enriched column types.

Details

Dates remain in years. Missing death times denote people alive at the recorded endpoint. Group columns are omitted when persons has no group column; otherwise their types are preserved. Groups are reconstructed at each union's start from retained transitions; later moves do not relabel earlier unions. A transition at the exact formation time follows formation, so its origin group applies. Without transition history, use recorded person groups. Existing columns whose names conflict with added partner fields cause an error.

Examples

population <- create_baseline_population(10)
get_detailed_unions(population)
#> # A tibble: 0 × 10
#> # ℹ 10 variables: union_id <int>, wife_id <int>, husband_id <int>,
#> #   start_time <dbl>, end_time <dbl>, end_reason <chr>, birth_time_w <dbl>,
#> #   death_time_w <dbl>, birth_time_h <dbl>, death_time_h <dbl>
